correctness.rationale: The analytic matrix element formula is correctly normalized by polar t=|z|^2 and the Fock basis. The disk top eigenvalue is simple with explicit gap exp(-R) S_m. The trace-class C^2 shape family legitimizes isolated-eigenvalue perturbation, including the positive eigenvector-mixing term; Parseval gives the exact Hessian. The falling-factorial ratio proves strictly ordered multipliers and a sharp quadrupole constant. Dominated convergence and lower finite-sum bounds prove the high-area transition in all alpha regimes. Direct quadrature checks corroborate normalizations but are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Full accessible text of Ramos 2026 and the relevant sections of Gómez–Guerra–Ramos–Tilli 2024, Nicola–Tilli 2022, and Nicola–Riccardi 2025 were compared for identical objects, equivalences, and stronger implications. Ramos shows local-maximizer disk rigidity and order-two examples, not the full shape Hessian. Gómez et al. compute the curvature of a different function-superlevel functional, with S_{m-1}, not the fixed-domain top-eigenvalue factor S_{m-1}/S_m. Neither Hilbert–Schmidt localization nor global disk optimality implies the asserted exact multipliers or transition. published-finding corpus returned related but distinct problems, not a covering claim; an unindexed duplication remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed older shape-variation computation might independently contain some coefficients; database absence is not proof of uniqueness.
The high-area transition is asserted only for Hessian multipliers, not simultaneous nonlinearly deformed domains.

value.rationale: Area-constrained shape stability for optimal Gaussian STFT concentration is natural following the sharp global disk theorem and its 2026 local-rigidity strengthening. The full Hessian identifies the complete distortion-frequency penalty, exact least-stable nontranslation mode and coefficient, and the m~R resolution transition. These are precise spectral design and quantitative local rigidity data not determined by mere uniqueness of the maximizing disk.
